body.intro: 48 statements in 8 areas. Answer how true each one is today. Takes 60 to 90 minutes; you can pause and come back.

areas.title: Strategy and direction
areas.plain: Do you know where the business is going, and does everyone else?

areas.title: Sales and pipeline
areas.plain: Is new business predictable, or does it depend on you?

areas.title: Customers and market
areas.plain: Do you know who buys, why, and who else they could buy from?

areas.title: Finance and cash
areas.plain: Can you see cash and margin before they become a problem?

areas.title: Operations and delivery
areas.plain: Does the business deliver without heroics?

areas.title: People and roles
areas.plain: Does everyone know their job and how it is judged?

areas.title: Leadership and governance
areas.plain: Are you working on the business, with a rhythm and a record?

areas.title: Risk and resilience
areas.plain: Could you survive a bad month, a lost supplier or a lost laptop?

questions.text: We can state in one sentence what the business will look like in three years
We have written down three to five priorities for this year
Every senior person can name those priorities without looking them up
We know which customers and products we deliberately do not pursue
Each priority has a measurable target and a named owner
We review progress against the plan at least quarterly
We know our monthly revenue target and where we stand against it every week
Every open opportunity is written down with a value, stage and next step
We know our conversion rate from first meeting to closed deal
New business does not depend on the owner personally selling
We follow a defined sales process with stages everyone uses the same way
We have enough qualified pipeline to hit next quarter's target
We can name our three most profitable customer types
We know why customers choose us over the alternatives, in their words
No single customer is more than 25% of our revenue
We measure customer satisfaction or repeat business in some regular way
We know who our main competitors are and how our prices compare
We have a clear offer we can explain to a new prospect in two minutes
We see a cash flow forecast for at least the next 13 weeks
We know our gross margin by product or service line
Management accounts are available within 15 days of month end
We know our break-even monthly revenue
Debtors are collected on average within our agreed terms
We have a budget for the year and compare actuals to it monthly
Our core delivery process is documented well enough for a new person to follow
We deliver on time and to spec in most cases and we measure it
We know our cost to deliver one unit of our main product or service
Key suppliers have agreed terms and a backup option
Our systems (accounting, CRM, job tracking) hold the data we need without manual re-typing
Problems in delivery are logged and fixed at the root, not just patched
Every person has a written role with the results they are accountable for
We know who would step up if a key person left tomorrow
Performance is reviewed against agreed goals at least twice a year
We can hire for a role within 60 days when we need to
Staff turnover in the past year was at a level we are comfortable with
People get the training they need to do their jobs well
The owner spends most of the week on the business, not in it
There is a leadership team that meets on a fixed rhythm with an agenda
Decisions above a set value or risk follow an agreed approval route
We have an outside voice (board, advisor, mentor) who challenges us
Statutory and tax filings are up to date
Important decisions and their reasons are recorded somewhere
We have listed the top risks to the business with their likelihood and impact
Each major risk has a named owner and a mitigation action
We could operate for a month if our main site, system or supplier failed
Insurance cover was reviewed in the past 12 months
Customer and company data is backed up and access is controlled
Issues that arise are logged, prioritised and tracked to closure

interpretation.label: Critical
interpretation.advice: Fix the basics in this area before anything else.

interpretation.label: Weak
interpretation.advice: A likely priority for the year.

interpretation.label: Strong
interpretation.advice: Keep it; measure it on the scorecard.
